question: Should the experiment-gated Claw lifecycle ownership model become a supported core Doctor surface once its prerequisite ownership layer lands?
rationale: The patch is technically bounded and has direct runtime proof, but only maintainers can decide whether this RFC-defined lifecycle model belongs in core, what upgrade behavior is acceptable for experimental users, and whether the stacked ownership contract should be supported long term.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core diagnostic
options.body: Land the prerequisite ownership PR first, then accept this non-mutating experimental Doctor surface with its warning and upgrade contract explicitly documented.

options.title: Defer the stacked Claws direction
options.body: Keep this PR open but unmerged until maintainers evaluate the RFC stack and decide whether core should own lifecycle diagnostics.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close the stack if maintainers do not want Claw lifecycle ownership and reconciliation to become a core OpenClaw capability.

recommendation.title: Defer the stacked Claws direction
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but unmerged until maintainers evaluate the RFC stack and decide whether core should own lifecycle diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature-history trail most closely connects shared-state and Doctor contract decisions to this owner.
